title: Power Pages: security agent in design studio configures authentication and authorisation
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap dates, approval requirement, governance paths and scan API match the sources checked. It distinguishes the preview from the planned general release and appropriately leaves security-agent-specific licensing and controls unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licensing model specific to this security agent.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages security agent licensing billing Copilot Credits consumption pricing; "Power Pages" "security agent" "license". Read security-agent, faq-security-agent, assign-licensing and the Power Platform licensing FAQ; no security-agent licensing model found.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The roadmap and preview feature documentation state no separate security-agent licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "security agent" "license". Read roadmap 577809, security/security-agent and faq-security-agent; none states a separate licence.

claims.claim: No security-agent-specific meter or credit charge is stated in the roadmap or preview Learn article.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "security agent" "billing"; Power Pages security agent licensing billing Copilot Credits consumption pricing. Read roadmap, security-agent, FAQ and platform licensing FAQ; no applicable security-agent charge found.

claims.claim: General-availability security-agent pricing and its consumption model are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages security agent licensing billing Copilot Credits consumption pricing; "Power Pages" "security agent" "billing". Read feature overview, FAQ, assign-licensing and platform licensing FAQ; no GA security-agent price or consumption model found.

claims.claim: The cited Power Pages licensing page covers subscriptions for the underlying site.
claims.quote: As you work on projects and need to establish permanent sites that don't expire, you can apply Power Pages subscriptions and convert websites from trial to production.

claims.claim: The cited Power Pages licensing page states no security-agent-specific entitlement.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "security agent" "license". Read assign-licensing in full and searched the linked Power Platform licensing FAQ for security agent; neither names a security-agent entitlement.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: The security agent is an AI-powered maker assistant embedded in the Power Pages design studio Security workspace.
claims.quote: Security agent is an AI-powered assistant built into the Power Pages Security workspace that helps makers review, configure, and strengthen the security of their Power Pages sites by using natural language.

claims.claim: Makers open the Security agent tab to access an embedded chat panel.
claims.quote: Makers can open the security agent tab to access the embedded chat panel and security tools.

claims.claim: Makers interact in natural language to review risks, understand configurations and take guided actions.
claims.quote: The agent analyzes your site's configuration, explains its findings, and proposes configuration changes where appropriate.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The agent can configure authentication providers and troubleshoot authentication.
claims.quote: Configure authentication providers, validate authentication settings, and diagnose common sign-in problems.

claims.claim: The agent can create and update web roles.
claims.quote: The agent helps create and update web roles, page permissions, and table permissions.

claims.claim: The agent can create and update table permissions.
claims.quote: The agent helps create and update web roles, page permissions, and table permissions.

claims.claim: The agent can create and update page permissions.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Every configuration change requires maker approval before the agent applies it.
claims.quote: For any configuration changes, the agent always requests your approval before making updates, so you remain in control of your site's security.

claims.claim: The agent confirms what it updated after execution.
claims.quote: Before applying any change, it requests your approval and, once complete, confirms exactly what was updated.

claims.claim: The preview documentation groups support into four primary security scenarios.
claims.quote: Security agent supports four primary security scenarios that cover the core areas of Power Pages site protection.

claims.claim: The agent's security posture review analyses configuration and vulnerability scan findings.
claims.quote: The agent analyzes authentication settings, authorization configuration, security settings, vulnerability scan findings, and site configuration

claims.claim: Supported authentication technologies include Microsoft Entra ID, OpenID Connect and SAML 2.0.
claims.quote: The agent supports Microsoft Entra ID, OpenID Connect, and SAML 2.0, and recommends configuration updates to resolve authentication problems.

claims.claim: The agent can review and configure Content Security Policy.
claims.quote: Review and configure application-level security settings including Content Security Policy (CSP)

claims.quote: Review and configure application-level security settings including Content Security Policy (CSP), HTTP security headers

claims.claim: The agent can review and configure CORS settings.
claims.quote: Review and configure application-level security settings including Content Security Policy (CSP), HTTP security headers, CORS

claims.claim: The agent can review and configure cookie settings.
claims.quote: Review and configure application-level security settings including Content Security Policy (CSP), HTTP security headers, CORS, cookie settings

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The agent can configure session controls.
claims.quote: Review and configure application-level security settings including Content Security Policy (CSP), HTTP security headers, CORS, cookie settings, session management, and WAF-related configurations.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The Learn article remains prerelease documentation for a preview feature.
claims.quote: [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.] Important: This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: The preview is not meant for production use.
claims.quote: Preview features aren’t meant for production use and might have restricted functionality.

claims.claim: Power Pages sites serve external or anonymous audiences.
claims.quote: Anonymous access to Dataverse tables shows the number of websites where anonymous access is allowed for certain tables in Microsoft Dataverse.

claims.claim: Overly permissive table permissions can expose data.
claims.quote: Check whether sensitive Dataverse tables are exposed through overly permissive permissions.

claims.claim: The agent helps makers without deep security expertise configure secure access.
claims.quote: It combines scheduled vulnerability scanning, real-time traffic anomaly detection, and guided remediation to assist non-security-expert makers in maintaining a secure posture.

claims.claim: Recommendations draw on the site's configuration and permissions.
claims.quote: It explains existing authorization settings and recommends least-privilege access based on your site's configuration.

claims.claim: The planned agent uses the site's data schema in its access recommendations.
claims.quote: Using the site’s data schema and usage patterns, it suggests appropriate access levels, such as read-only, owner-only, or full administrative control aligned with least privilege best practices.

claims.claim: The agent is designed to recommend least-privilege access.
claims.quote: It explains existing authorization settings and recommends least-privilege access based on your site's configuration.

claims.claim: AI recommendations are not a guarantee of correct configuration.
claims.quote: AI-generated suggestions may occasionally be overly conservative or not applicable to complex edge cases.

claims.quote: Use Security agent in development or test environments before promoting changes to production.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout

claims.quote: Validate and deploy approved changes using your organization's standard ALM process.

claims.claim: The tenant setting is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Tenant settings > Publish Copilots with AI features.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Manage. In the Manage pane, select Tenant settings. Publish Copilots with AI features | Allows Copilot authors to publish from Copilot Studio when AI features are enabled.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for the Publish Copilots with AI features tenant switch is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Publish Copilots with AI features tenant settings PowerShell Set-TenantSettings API publish bots generative ai; "Publish Copilots with AI features" "API". Read tenant-settings and list-tenantsettings search excerpt; the latter's enableOpenAiBotPublishing is explicitly unused.

claims.claim: The publishing tenant control governs site chatbot publishing.
claims.quote: Chat agent (site Copilot) specific setting: If the setting for “Publish bots with AI” is disabled at the tenant level, admins are unable to configure site Copilot at the environment level.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that the chatbot publishing control applies to the security agent.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages security agent disable switch roles privileges audit approval logs chat start scan; "Publish Copilots with AI features" "API". Read security-agent, FAQ, tenant-settings and copilot-hub; no security-agent applicability stated.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Power Pages AI settings are at Power Platform admin center > Copilot Hub > Power Pages > Settings.
claims.quote: To view or update these settings, navigate to Copilot hub > Power Pages > Settings in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Copilot hub controls whether makers in specific environments can use AI features.
claims.quote: Enable or disable AI features for makers Control whether makers in specific environments can use AI features.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for the per-environment Power Pages maker AI feature control is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Copilot hub environment maker AI features settings API PowerShell pac admin Dataverse; "Power Pages" "Copilot" "API" "settings" "maker". Read copilot-hub; its PowerShell mention concerns tenant site-user settings, not the environment maker control.

claims.where: controls[3]; controls[1].note; Governance controls table and prose; Open questions
claims.claim: A separate switch specific to the security chat agent is not documented on the UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages security agent enable disable tenant environment Dataverse Web API Power Platform API pac pages; "Power Pages" "security agent" "disable". Read security-agent, FAQ, copilot-hub and pac power-pages excerpts; no separate chat-agent switch found.

claims.claim: The feature documentation does not specify the roles or privileges required to use the security agent.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages security agent disable switch roles privileges audit approval logs chat start scan; "Power Pages" "security agent" "roles". Read security-agent and faq-security-agent in full; neither specifies an access role or privilege.

claims.claim: The site security scan UI is in Power Pages design studio > Security workspace > Run scan.
claims.quote: Use the Security workspace to run the scan. After you receive the email confirmation, you can view the scan report summary by returning to the Run scan section of the Security workspace.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: POST https://api.powerplatform.com/powerpages/environments/{environmentId}/websites/{id}/scan/deep/start?api-version=2024-10-01 starts a website deep scan.
claims.quote: Start deep scan for a Power Pages website. POST https://api.powerplatform.com/powerpages/environments/{environmentId}/websites/{id}/scan/deep/start?api-version=2024-10-01

claims.claim: Copilot hub manages Power Pages Copilot governance, replacing the deprecated tenant-level governance configuration.
claims.quote: The tenant-level governance configuration feature is now deprecated. While your existing settings will remain in place, we strongly recommend reviewing and validating them to ensure they still meet your requirements.

claims.claim: The older generative-AI governance control covered site-user experiences, not maker experiences.
claims.quote: As an administrator, you can choose to disable Generative AI features for your website users. The following AI-powered experiences are governed separately and are not covered by this control: Site copilot; Maker experiences.

claims.claim: The FAQ describes a wider security-agent system that includes scheduled vulnerability scanning.
claims.quote: It combines scheduled vulnerability scanning, real-time traffic anomaly detection, and guided remediation to assist non-security-expert makers in maintaining a secure posture.

claims.claim: A chat command that starts a security scan is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "security agent" "scan" "prompt". Read security-agent, faq-security-agent, security-scan and use-security-workspace; documented chat prompts analyse findings, while scan initiation is documented separately.

claims.claim: Administrators can initiate scans from the Power Platform admin center security pages.
claims.quote: Site-specific details, including the scan status, scan score (number of passed/failed checks), if the scan is completed, a view of the scan results, and an option to initiate the scan.

claims.claim: The security assistant is aimed at people configuring and securing sites, rather than at site visitors.
claims.quote: Security agent is an AI-powered assistant built into the Power Pages Security workspace that helps makers review, configure, and strengthen the security of their Power Pages sites by using natural language.
